A revolving frame is equipped with several key components, including a counterweight, an engine, a cooling fan, a heat exchanger, an exterior cover, and an exhaust gas purifying device. These components are arranged so that the engine and related equipment can be efficiently cooled and protected while the machine operates.

The exhaust gas purifying device is configured to reduce harmful emissions from the engine. It includes a urea selective reduction catalyst and a urea water injection valve. The urea water injection valve is positioned upstream of the urea selective reduction catalyst and injects urea water into the exhaust gas before the gas reaches the catalyst. This allows the urea water to react with the exhaust gas in the catalyst, thereby reducing nitrogen oxides contained in the exhaust gas.

A urea water supply line is connected to the urea water injection valve. This supply line carries urea water from a urea water source to the injection valve, ensuring that the required amount of urea water can be supplied for exhaust gas purification.

On the front side of the counterweight, a horizontal support member is provided. This horizontal support member supports the exterior cover and helps maintain the structural arrangement of the components around the engine compartment.

A heat shield cover is mounted on the horizontal support member. The heat shield cover defines a line accommodating space in which the urea water supply line is housed. By accommodating the urea water supply line within this space, the heat shield cover protects the line from heat generated by the engine. As a result, the urea water supply line can be routed near the engine while being shielded from excessive heat, helping to maintain reliable supply of urea water to the injection valve and stable operation of the exhaust gas purifying device.

A revolving-frame machine is provided with an engine mounted on a revolving frame, cooling components for cooling the engine, and an exhaust gas purifying device disposed in an exhaust passage of the engine. The exhaust gas purifying device includes a urea selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalyst configured to reduce nitrogen oxides contained in exhaust gas. A urea water supply system is also provided for supplying urea water to the exhaust gas purifying device.

The revolving frame includes a horizontal support member positioned in the vicinity of a counterweight. A heat shield cover is mounted to this horizontal support member. The heat shield cover is arranged so as to block or reduce the transfer of heat from the engine and the exhaust system toward surrounding components. In particular, the heat shield cover forms, together with the horizontal support member, a protected space extending along the support member.

A urea water supply line, which forms part of the urea water supply system, is arranged inside this protected space between the horizontal support member and the heat shield cover. By housing the urea water supply line in this space, the supply line is shielded from radiant heat and hot air generated by the engine, the exhaust manifold, and the exhaust gas purifying device. This arrangement helps prevent excessive temperature rise of the urea water flowing through the line.

As a result, deterioration, crystallization, or vapor-lock-related problems in the urea water supply line can be suppressed. The urea water can therefore be supplied more stably to the urea SCR catalyst. This improves the operating reliability of the urea water supply system and contributes to stable purification of exhaust gas. In addition, because the protected space is formed using the existing horizontal support member and the heat shield cover mounted near the counterweight, the urea water supply line can be protected without requiring a complicated structure or a large increase in the number of parts.

Accordingly, the machine achieves improved heat protection for the urea water supply line, enhanced durability of the exhaust purification components, and increased reliability of the exhaust gas purifying device while maintaining an efficient layout within the limited space of the revolving frame.
outputs.L5:
**On a Revolving World**

On a revolving world, nothing stays exactly where it was. The Earth turns quietly beneath our feet, carrying cities, oceans, forests, and deserts from dawn into dusk and back again. We often feel still, as if the ground is fixed and unmoving, yet we are always in motion—spinning through space, circling the sun, and moving with the rhythm of time.

A revolving motion can remind us of life itself. Days repeat, seasons return, and familiar moments come back in new forms. Morning follows night, spring follows winter, and each turn brings both change and renewal. What seems like an ending may simply be another point in the cycle.

On a revolving wheel, every point rises and falls. In the same way, people experience success and difficulty, joy and uncertainty. No position is permanent. This can be comforting: hard times pass, and new opportunities appear as life continues to turn.

To live on a revolving planet is to understand movement, balance, and change. We may not control every rotation, but we can choose how we move with it. Each day offers another turn, another chance, and another beginning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the construction of a hydraulic excavator machine room including the urea SCR catalyst, urea water injection valve, supply line, horizontal support member, and heat shield cover.
counterfactuals.output:
A hydraulic excavator machine room is constructed to house the engine and exhaust-gas purification equipment while protecting the urea water system from heat and vibration.

The machine room includes an engine compartment in which an engine is mounted on the revolving upper structure of the excavator. An exhaust pipe connected to the engine leads exhaust gas to a urea SCR catalyst, which is arranged in the machine room as part of the exhaust aftertreatment system. The urea SCR catalyst reduces nitrogen oxides in the exhaust gas by using ammonia generated from injected urea water.

A urea water injection valve is mounted on the exhaust passage upstream of the urea SCR catalyst. The injection valve injects urea water into the exhaust gas flowing toward the SCR catalyst. The injected urea water is decomposed by exhaust heat to form ammonia, which then reacts with NOx in the SCR catalyst.

A urea water supply line extends from a urea water tank or supply module to the urea water injection valve. The supply line is routed through the machine room while being kept away from high-temperature components such as the exhaust pipe, engine, and catalyst casing as much as possible. The line supplies pressurized urea water to the injection valve.

A horizontal support member is provided in the machine room, for example as a frame, bracket, or beam extending generally horizontally. This support member supports or guides components such as the urea water supply line, wiring, clamps, or auxiliary brackets. It also serves as a mounting base for protective structures.

A heat shield cover is arranged between the high-temperature exhaust aftertreatment components and the urea water supply line or injection-related components. The heat shield cover is supported by the horizontal support member and covers at least part of the urea SCR catalyst, exhaust pipe, or the region near the urea water injection valve. Its purpose is to block radiant heat and reduce heat transfer to the urea water supply line and surrounding components.

In this construction, the urea SCR catalyst and injection valve are placed within the machine room near the engine exhaust system, while the urea water supply line is supported and protected along the horizontal support member. The heat shield cover prevents excessive heating of the urea water and associated parts, improving durability and maintaining stable urea injection performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style description of an exhaust gas purifying device arrangement where a urea water supply line is protected from engine heat by being accommodated between a support member and a heat shield cover.
counterfactuals.output:
**Exhaust Gas Purifying Device Arrangement**

An exhaust gas purifying device arrangement is provided for an internal combustion engine, the arrangement being configured to suppress thermal influence on a urea water supply line while maintaining compactness and ease of assembly.

The arrangement includes an exhaust gas purifying device disposed in an exhaust passage of the engine and configured to purify exhaust gas discharged from the engine. The exhaust gas purifying device may include, for example, a selective catalytic reduction catalyst for reducing nitrogen oxides contained in the exhaust gas by using ammonia generated from urea water. A urea water injection device is provided for supplying urea water into the exhaust passage upstream of the selective catalytic reduction catalyst. The urea water injection device is connected to a urea water tank by a urea water supply line through which urea water is delivered.

A support member is provided adjacent to the engine or adjacent to the exhaust gas purifying device. The support member supports at least one component of the exhaust gas purifying device arrangement, such as the urea water injection device, an exhaust pipe, a catalyst casing, a bracket, or a related accessory component. A heat shield cover is mounted to the support member or to a structure near the support member. The heat shield cover is arranged between the engine and the urea water supply line so as to block radiant heat from the engine and/or from an exhaust system component.

The urea water supply line is accommodated in a space defined between the support member and the heat shield cover. In other words, the urea water supply line is routed along the support member and is covered, at least partially, by the heat shield cover. The support member and the heat shield cover cooperate to form a protective passage or shielded region for the urea water supply line. As a result, the urea water supply line is protected from heat generated by the engine and from radiant heat emitted by high-temperature exhaust components.

The heat shield cover may be formed from a metallic plate material, a heat-resistant resin material, or a laminated insulating material. The cover may include a bent or recessed portion that defines a receiving space for the urea water supply line. The support member may include a substantially flat mounting surface, a channel-shaped portion, a rib, a flange, or a guide portion for positioning the urea water supply line. The urea water supply line may be held by clips, clamps, grommets, or retaining portions provided on the support member or the heat shield cover.

By locating the urea water supply line between the support member and the heat shield cover, the supply line can be thermally protected without requiring a separate dedicated heat insulating pipe or an additional protective bracket. This arrangement reduces the number of components, improves mountability, and enables the urea water supply line to be routed close to the exhaust gas purifying device while reducing the risk of thermal deterioration, vapor lock, crystallization, or damage to the line.

In one embodiment, the heat shield cover is fixed to the support member by fastening members such as bolts, screws, or clips, and the urea water supply line is disposed inward of the fastening portions. The heat shield cover may extend in a longitudinal direction of the urea water supply line so that a predetermined length of the supply line is covered. The cover may also include openings or cutout portions through which the supply line enters and exits the shielded space.

In another embodiment, the support member is disposed on a side of the urea water supply line opposite the engine, and the heat shield cover is disposed on the engine side of the urea water supply line. Accordingly, radiant heat from the engine is intercepted by the heat shield cover before reaching the urea water supply line. The support member further serves as a structural backing member and may also shield the supply line from heat transmitted from surrounding components.

According to this arrangement, the urea water supply line is efficiently protected from engine heat by utilizing an existing support structure and a heat shield cover. The arrangement provides improved durability and reliability of the urea water supply system while allowing the exhaust gas purifying device to be installed in a limited engine compartment space.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a detailed one-paragraph explanation of an invention involving a revolving frame, counterweight, engine, cooling fan, heat exchanger, exterior cover, SCR catalyst, urea injection valve, and protected urea water supply line.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a compact exhaust-aftertreatment and cooling arrangement for an engine mounted on, or operatively associated with, a revolving frame, such as the upper rotating structure of a construction machine, in which the engine is installed near a counterweight and is cooled by a cooling fan that draws or drives air through a heat exchanger while the exterior of the assembly is enclosed by an exterior cover. An SCR catalyst is disposed in an exhaust passage of the engine to reduce nitrogen oxides in the exhaust gas, and a urea injection valve is positioned upstream of the SCR catalyst so that urea water can be injected into the exhaust stream and converted to ammonia for selective catalytic reduction. A urea water supply line extends from a urea tank or supply source to the urea injection valve, and the line is routed within a protected region defined by the revolving frame, counterweight, engine, heat exchanger, cooling fan, and/or exterior cover so that it is shielded from flying debris, external impact, excessive heat, and environmental exposure. By arranging the supply line along an inner side of the exterior cover or behind structural components such as the counterweight and frame members, while also keeping it away from high-temperature exhaust portions and, where appropriate, within the cooling airflow generated by the fan, the invention prevents freezing, overheating, rupture, and accidental damage of the urea water line. This configuration improves reliability of the SCR system, maintains stable delivery of urea water to the injection valve, supports efficient exhaust purification, and allows the engine, cooling system, counterweight, and aftertreatment components to be packaged efficiently within the limited space of the revolving frame without compromising serviceability or protection.
